review_type: Independent cross-review; not a blinded or fresh-context benchmark
mode: Audit only; artifact source was not edited
input_boundary: Read the supplied HTML, original reading brief, indicated skill resources and actual browser observations. No artifact handoffs, author conclusions, prior evaluation notes or other case artifacts were read.
summary: The normal desktop and mobile views support the supplied reading task. No unsupported instance of the 19 checklist signals or the two additional ornamental defaults was found in the inspected UI or SVG artwork. One responsive typography issue remains in mobile details under enlarged text.

remaining_issues.condition: 390×844, HTML text and inputs at 200% of their computed font sizes; SVG covers remain unchanged
remaining_issues.observation: The detail grid keeps a 100px cover and 18px gap, leaving about 194px for the enlarged title. A Map of Small Distances breaks Distances into Distance / s; Ways of Making and Remaking a Home breaks Remaking into Remakin / g. The long title also pushes the reading-state choices below the initial modal viewport.
remaining_issues.consequence: Important identifying text becomes harder to read, and moving a long-title book requires extra modal scrolling. overflow-wrap:anywhere prevents horizontal overflow but does not resolve the cramped relationship.
remaining_issues.correction: At this narrow content width or enlarged text setting, let the title and author span the full detail width and stack or relocate the cover. Preserve the full text and native scrolling; recheck b2 and b4 at the same condition without reducing the enlarged type.
remaining_issues.functional_boundary: The dialog scrolls and the state action remained reachable and successful for all four enlarged details; Escape and sensible focus return also passed. This is an arrangement/readability issue, not a lost control or horizontal overflow.
remaining_issues.signal_relationship: No negative tracking is present. This finding concerns the coupled cover/title layout rather than a forbidden font or ornamental signal.

signal_review.observation_and_reason: The filters and state choices are unboxed text controls with real selected state; shelf state is a plain label. Counts were verified after every state change. Keep the useful status and selection meaning.
No decorative italic headline or cover accents appear. The SVG titles and authors use upright Georgia.
Instrument Serif is not used. System sans-serif carries the interface; Georgia is confined to the wordmark and actual book-cover typography. No font replacement is indicated.
No negative letter spacing is authored or visible. The enlarged-title issue is caused by a narrow fixed grid relationship, not tracking; it is reported separately as R1.
The UI contains the actual search, filters, books, facts and state controls requested by the brief. There are no fake analytics, reviews, ratings or inactive demonstration controls.
There are no repeated section rules. The short underline beneath a selected filter or state communicates actual selection, and remains worth keeping.

Body, secondary text and action colors have distinct roles. Sample interface contrasts are strong. The translucent backdrop communicates modality; the cover palettes belong to the individual artwork rather than a ladder of faded UI labels.
The search-field border identifies an input, and focus outlines identify keyboard position. Books are not enclosed in repeated bordered cards. Preserve these working boundaries.
The b2 cover uses a small, simple street-grid illustration tied to A Map of Small Distances. It is artwork, not a fake system diagram or a replacement for product evidence.

The compact tagline, search label, recovery copy and fictional-data notices have distinct jobs. Title/author repetition in printed cover artwork plus HTML labels preserves both cover identity and readable accessible book labels; it is not repeated interface framing.
No file paths, version strings or code-themed text decorate the customer flow.
No ornamental sequence numbers occur. Book counts and page totals are factual values.

Find a book labels the search input, and Reading state labels its choice group. These are useful form orientation, not repeated introductory scaffolding. The Essays text in b1 artwork states the supplied genre.
No ASCII or terminal-style imagery occurs.

The map, botanical form and doorway are simple cover illustrations tied to their book subjects. The botanical curves depict a plant; they are not unassigned doodles, emphasis marks or loose ornamental squiggles.
No monospace typography is used. UI reading remains in the system sans-serif stack.
Supporting labels, titles and SVG cover text use ordinary title or sentence case. No repeated small uppercase scaffold appears.
Surfaces and covers use solid fills. There are no ambient gradients or haze behind text.
Short action and filter labels have no ornamental periods. Sentence punctuation in notes and feedback, and the initials N. K. Adeyemi in HTML and SVG, preserve necessary language.
There are no decorative round status, demo, availability or brand lights. Actual reading state is expressed in words and selected controls.

signal_review.signal: Additional default: arrow glyphs and icons
signal_review.observation_and_reason: No ordinary action, row, cover or caption carries an appended arrow or chevron. The SVG map and doorway contain no arrow motif.

significant_exceptions_kept.treatment: Selected-state underlines and real reading-state text
significant_exceptions_kept.reason: They communicate the active filter or actual book state; removing them would weaken the central task.

significant_exceptions_kept.treatment: Search border and visible focus outlines
significant_exceptions_kept.reason: These are actual input and keyboard affordances, not fragmented content containers.

significant_exceptions_kept.treatment: Upright serif cover type, street grid, botanical shape and doorway
significant_exceptions_kept.reason: The brief explicitly asks for original typographic covers or simple SVG artwork. These motifs identify the supplied fictional books and do not add generic arrows, lights, italics or unassigned marks.
They preserve truthful demo boundaries in the shelf and detail contexts.

actual_checks.enlarged_text_method: 200% computed font sizes applied to actual HTML text nodes and inputs, including dynamically populated detail text and recreated choices; SVG artwork remains proportionally intact. This is a text stress test, not a full browser zoom audit.
actual_checks.overflow_result: No horizontal page overflow at either requested size, normal or enlarged; enlarged dialog clientWidth and scrollWidth were both 352px on mobile. Vertical dialog scrolling remains available.
actual_checks.contrast_boundary: Opaque solid-color calculations only, not a complete accessibility or artwork contrast audit.
actual_checks.svg_review: Viewed all four covers in shelf and detail contexts at desktop and mobile. Inspected SVG text and path content for italic accents, negative tracking, arrows, lights, generic decorative diagrams, gradients and unassigned marks.

limits: Headless Chromium only; no physical device, other browser engine or screen-reader audit.
Text enlargement was a controlled CSS stress test rather than actual browser zoom.
No claim of complete accessibility or production verification.
No edits, external network use, delegation or publication were performed.
publicationNote: Substantive observations retained; local paths normalized. Audit findings concern the preserved pre-repair snapshot; repair verification concerns the corrected example.
